legal_foundation: Land and Conveyancing Law Reform Act 2009 Part 10
verified_facts: Tailte Éireann provides Form 17 for an application for registration of a mortgage/loan charge and requires the charge to identify the lender and property, with a folio reference.
Tailte Éireann provides Forms 51 and 52 for specified registered-land charges under the Land Registration Rules 2012.
Tailte Éireann lists procedures for transfer and cancellation/release of charges, including Forms 56, 57A, 57B and 58.
Tailte Éireann identifies judgment mortgages as a separate registration category.

For charges dated on or after 1 December 2009, Tailte Éireann states that a mortgagee's power of sale is subject to the statutory court-order/consent framework under section 100(3) of the Land and Conveyancing Law Reform Act 2009.
guardrails: A registered charge is not the same thing as ownership.
A mortgage balance cannot be inferred from the mere existence of a folio entry.
A charge entry must be interpreted with its legal basis and relevant documents.
Mortgage enforcement is distinct from ordinary ownership transfer.
Co-ownership, succession and mortgage interests must be analysed together where they intersect.
Do not state that a mortgagee can sell property without checking the applicable date, statutory framework and required court order or consent.
